title: Confluence unauthorized-admin and curl exfiltration safe Ubuntu slice

source.confidence_notes: The advisory reports exploitation that creates unauthorized Confluence administrator accounts and observes curl or Rclone for exfiltration. This package does not exploit Confluence or create an operating-system account. It uses an application-audit canary, fake staged text, and a loopback-only HTTP receiver.

initial_alert.text: An unexpected application administrator event was followed by a multipart HTTP upload. Investigate the Ubuntu endpoint and reconstruct the sequence.

steps.name: Write a harmless Confluence administrator audit canary
Stage fake text and upload it to a loopback Mock service with curl
steps.atomic_name: Exfiltrate staged file to a Discord webhook with curl (bash)
steps.cleanup_action: Atomic cleanup removes staged-loot.txt; exact-root cleanup removes mock-exfil.json

expected_findings.expected: confluence-audit.json records a harmless administrator-account canary for benchmark_admin
staged-loot.txt contains only the Atomic fake-data marker
expected_findings.temporal_relation: created after the audit canary and before upload

expected_findings.expected: the loopback Mock service records one POST /upload request containing the fake-data marker
audit canary timestamp is no later than staged-file time, which is no later than Mock upload time
expected_findings.temporal_relation: application event precedes staging and upload

omitted_behaviors: Creation of a real Confluence or Linux administrator account
Use of real credentials, victim content, Rclone, or cloud storage
Connections to public indicators or any non-loopback address
Installation of malicious plugins or additional persistence
